status: EXPERIMENTAL synthesis. Not a public claim. Each theme links back to track findings; the track finding, not this file, is the evidence.

partial: V1-verification (verdicts.json: A-F-01, A-F-03, A-F-07, A-F-08 so far)

agreement.corroborate: two or more tracks reach the same conclusion from different data or methods
agreement.contradict: tracks state incompatible facts, or one track's data refutes another track's inference or framing
agreement.independent: related findings that neither support nor refute each other; listed so readers do not mistake adjacency for corroboration

strength.strong: at least two tracks, at least one VERIFIED, from separate data sources or methods
strength.moderate: two tracks, but SUPPORTED-only, or the same underlying source, or a partial overlap in scope
strength.weak: thematic overlap only, or rests on one INCONCLUSIVE/SUPPORTED finding

themes.theme: Praxis .ros state files are the dominant merge-conflict surface in multi-lane runs
themes.notes: A-F-07 (R8 coordinator log: 26/49 PR merges, all .ros only) and B-F-09 (git merge-tree replay of every two-parent merge: R8 56 of 60 conflicted merges .ros-only, R10 29 of 34) reach the same conclusion from different sources. V1 independently reproduced the 26/49 at PR level. A2's preregistration pre-scan (R8 58/60 touch .ros; R10 34/34 touch .ros) agrees. B ranks this mechanism 8 and recommends taking .ros out of the merge path (B REPORT section 5 item 5); A ranks it recommendation 4. See X-02 for the part of A-F-07 that does NOT hold.

themes.theme: Whether R8 had any application-code merge conflicts
themes.notes: A-F-07 states 'no application-code conflicts occurred in this rehearsal'. B-F-09 counts R8 as '4 source / 56 records-only of 87' and names Classify.fs and GitHubRequests.fs as conflicting in both R8 and R10. V1 rated A-F-07 PARTIALLY VERIFIED: the 26/49 PR-level count is right, but 4 'merge origin/main into lane' commits conflicted in 6 non-state paths (Program.fs, Classify.fs, GitHubRequests.fs, StatefulFake.fs, INV22.fs, live.yml). Cause: merges.jsonl logs only the coordinator's PR-merge step. Resolution: the .ros finding stands for the PR-merge step; the rehearsal-level 'no app-code conflicts' inference is contradicted by B and V1. Any ADR or outline must not repeat it. Denominator also differs: 26/49 PR merges (53%) vs 60/86-87 merge commits (70%); B says 87, V1 says 86 merge commits (unreconciled, minor).

themes.theme: Per-rehearsal merge-conflict counts differ between B and A2's pre-scan
themes.notes: B-F-09: R3 'no recorded merge commits', R5 17/92 conflicted (all source), R6 1/6 (.ros only). A2 pre-scan: R3 3 conflicts (none .ros), R5 15, R6 0. Both use git merge-tree over two-parent merges 'on all refs'. Likely causes: ref set fetched (B used 420-minute windows; A2 may include all history), merge-tree options. Low consequence for conclusions (both agree conflicts concentrate in multi-lane runs and in .ros for R8/R10), but any published conflict count must state window and ref set. Re-check when A2 publishes results.

themes.theme: Completion and acceptance are self-declared: verified completion is built but not enabled
themes.notes: E-F-01 (VERIFIED by execution: 0 of 45 ros.json files enable requireVerifiedCompletion/attestation; /etc/hostname accepted as tests) and G-F-07 (VERIFIED from Praxis 3.25.0 docs: 'Mandatory verified completion is not enabled across Echelon repositories') agree from different methods. E-F-06 shows the attested controls do work on 3.25.0 when enabled, so the gap is adoption, not capability. C-F-02 explains part of why: 23 repositories pin Praxis 3.7.2, which predates attested completion (3.20.0). C-F-04 is the same pattern one layer up (attested range qualification built but trust keys empty). G-F-09's commercial thesis (independent attested definition of done) therefore rests on a capability that the program does not itself use. Caveat: G-F-07's supporting status data is as of 2026-10-23; E's survey is current.

themes.theme: The 'computed verdict' ended self-declared acceptance only against an honest agent
themes.notes: Framing contradiction, not a data contradiction. B-F-04/B-F-15 present the computed verdict (from R4, OD-INDY-7) as the change that ended self-declared acceptance (observational, SUPPORTED). E-F-02 (VERIFIED) shows the computed verdict returns ACCEPTED for a fully fabricated 118-artifact bundle, because the 'independent' manifest pin in rehearsal-005's acceptance.sh is printed by the candidate's own tool in the same job. Both can be true: agents stopped over-claiming acceptance (behaviour), but the verdict mechanism would not have caught a dishonest or mistaken producer (control strength). B-F-04's own observation that over-claim moved to obligation over-tagging (R5: 13/22 spot-checked over-tagged) is exactly the input layer E-F-02 says is unverified. Publications must say 'agents stopped claiming acceptance' and must not say 'acceptance became verified'.

themes.theme: Status claims exceeding evidence recur at every layer: agents, verifiers, documentation, public site
themes.notes: Agent level: B-F-04, B-F-16 (R1 RC2-RC5 treated as Accepted while the deploy/accept workflow was red; Actions-confirmed), B-F-02 (R2 recomputes INVALID). Mechanism level: E-F-02 (fabricated acceptance), E-F-05 ('verified' label with zero evidence, labelled unattested), E-F-11, E-F-12. Documentation level: C-F-14 (READMEs contradicted by code), C-F-08 (Aegis 2.0.0 documented, never released). Public level: G-F-10 (site claims 40%+ throughput, 80% reconciliation reduction with no located evidence; INCONCLUSIVE). Moderate, not strong: the layers are different phenomena joined by one theme, and G-F-10 is INCONCLUSIVE (evidence may exist privately).

themes.theme: Toolchain/catalog defects recur across rehearsals; link to ecosystem pin staleness
themes.notes: The suggested pairing 'C-F-01 staleness explains B's recurring toolchain defects' only partly holds. The rehearsals that hit the defects (R8, R10, Causa) are on new sets, and C-F-01 says only causa and rehearsal-010 match the approved set; the stale repositories are libraries and tools, not rehearsals. The direct corroboration is narrower: B-F-13's forma-workflow-outside-approved-set (R4, R5, R8, R10) is the same fact as C-F-09 (forma-workflow qualified as a Conditor built-in with no Registry entry) and C-F-03 (two catalogs that disagree). The FSharp.Core central-package-management defect (R8, R10) has no C counterpart. The better causal story is churn plus dual catalogs (C-F-03, C-F-18: 12 owner-approved sets in 13 days), not staleness. Staleness (C-F-01) corroborates instead with X-04 (C-F-02: verified completion unreachable on 3.7.2).

themes.theme: CI waste is concentrated in harness-semantics failures (R6 starvation, R10 job cap)
themes.notes: A-F-12 (job-minute measure): R6 85% and R10 88% of CI minutes in failed/cancelled runs; A-F-11: R6 queue p90 912 s; A-F-14: R10 median commit latency 2,470 s. B-F-08 (run-list measure): R6 116/132 build-and-test runs cancelled (per-commit concurrency group plus if: always()); R10 20-minute cap against a ~29-minute browser suite. Different data (A jobs/steps, B run lists) and different units (A job-minutes, B run counts), same two outliers and same mechanisms. Excluding R6 and R10, A gets 38% red/cancelled. V1 is checking A-F-11/A-F-12 (pending).

themes.theme: Governance machinery first exercised inside the timed window is the terminal blocker from R8 on
themes.notes: B-F-03 is the primary evidence (10 of 11 runs; 29 of 116 failure events; one analyst's curation, so prevalence is ESTIMATE). Supporting angles: A-F-13 (governance tool rebuilt from source in every CI run, 688 min) shows governance cost inside the window; C-F-12 (39k-line parallel toolchain in Indy-init) explains why the gates are new each run; E-F-02 shows the gates that do run are not independent. No other track measured B's 'first exercised inside the window' claim directly. B2-dryrun is the direct test; re-assess when it lands.

themes.theme: Approval and owner-attestation authority is blurred
themes.notes: B-F-12/B-F-04: agents wrote approvals (R3, R4 on owner instruction), R8 INVALID on the approvals file, chat attestations do not count. E-F-07 (SUPPORTED with VERIFIED parts): agent token reported as admin, merges under owner login, no branch protection or CODEOWNERS. E-F-08: owner attestation keyed only on review login, so an agent-submitted review under the owner's credential would satisfy it (not executed). E-F-12: agents can record owner-approval evidence as a human (labelled unattested). Moderate: the credential facts behind E-F-07 come from the R7 audit, not from this sprint.

themes.theme: Process instructions and Echelon overhead cost more tokens without a measured quality gain on current fixtures
themes.notes: A-F-16 (new controlled pilots CONSTRUCT-008, time-entry-expanded-01: protocol arm +47%/+93% tokens at equal acceptance) and G-F-08 (REL-001: +35.5% per correct requirement) agree. D's recomputation of VAC-001 controls (Ordo/full Echelon +14% to +31% vs B) is consistent. Caution: A-F-16 also cites REL-001 and ARCH-002, which G-F-08 uses, so part of the corroboration is shared-source. The new pilots are n=3 per arm. Fixtures show ceiling effects (all arms correct), so 'no quality gain' is 'not detectable on these fixtures', not 'no gain'. A-F-05 (48.7k fixed prefix, ~30% of context; ESTIMATE) is the mechanism.

themes.theme: Coordinator context cap vs evidence that agent continuity is cheaper
findings: D:CLAIMS.md (VAC-001 B vs A -40.9%; DR vs D +85.7%)
themes.notes: A-F-03 (VERIFIED by V1 exactly) shows the R8 coordinator was 44% of tokens and 32% of cost at 3.6x task-agent context; A recommends capping its context by refreshing from a checkpoint (ESTIMATE: ~$30 saving). VAC-001, recomputed by D, found agent continuity cut cost per accepted requirement by ~41% versus fresh agents, and 'fresh-from-verified-state' cost +86% versus continuous (preliminary, one chain). These are different roles (coordinator vs implementer) and different scales (830k vs fixture context), so it is a tension rather than a refutation. But A's saving estimate assumes a refreshed coordinator does not re-pay startup and rediscovery cost; VAC-001 suggests that re-pay can dominate. The ADR on a context cap must treat the net saving as untested.

themes.theme: Inconsistent cost and acceptance units across tracks
themes.notes: Definitions conflict, not data. (1) Acceptance unit: A-F-02 uses passing criterion (R3), VERIFIED P0 requirement (R7), fully verified P0 requirement or obligation (R8); G-F-08/G-F-11 use 'correct requirement' on REL-001 fixtures; VAC-001 uses 'accepted requirement'; B-F-01 uses the run-level Indy-init verdict, under which no run was accepted. (2) Resulting scale gap: G-F-11 argues compute is not the binding constraint because cost is '$0.11-$0.16 per correct requirement on fixtures', while A measures $0.71-$3.80 per verified unit in rehearsals (5x-35x higher) and, under B-F-01's verdict, the cost per accepted requirement of a real rehearsal is undefined (zero accepted). G's conclusion (predictability, not compute, binds) may still hold, but its number should not be cited as the rehearsal cost. (3) Price basis: A's $193.74 uses the 5m/1h cache-write split; V1 notes $190.51 on a 5m-only basis, which is the basis A used for R3/R7; cross-rehearsal comparisons mix bases. (4) 'Cost per accepted requirement' is proposed by G-F-03 as an engagement metric, but no track has a definition of 'accepted' that survives E-F-02. Recommend a sprint-wide unit glossary before any publication.

themes.theme: Readiness of outcome-based delivery: G uses R1-R3, B has R1-R10
themes.notes: G-F-11 (CONTRADICTED hypothesis: managed factory not ready) and B-F-01 (no run R1-Causa accepted) agree on the conclusion. B extends G's three-run basis to eleven runs. One wording inconsistency: G-F-11 says 'Rehearsal 1 passed but with 25 defects'; B records R1 as self-classified PASS predating the ledger contract, with an Actions-confirmed acceptance over-claim (B-F-16). G's wording should be updated to B's.

themes.theme: Cross-rehearsal comparisons are confounded
themes.notes: A and B independently refuse to compare runs: scope, topology, units, T0 definition and stack all change. B-F-07 (VERIFIED: R6 imported R5's 99 source files byte for byte) invalidates any R5/R6 comparison, which affects A-F-12's R6 figure as a measure of R6's own process and B-F-10 milestones. D's note that VAC-001 bootstrap CIs treat within-chain units as independent is the same caution for controlled experiments. Consequence for publications: no improvement-over-time claim is supportable.

themes.theme: Live provider evidence in R10: B and E agree on what causa-acceptance-r10 is
themes.notes: B-F-14 (branch timestamps: 114 probe branches inside R10's window, so live tests ran in CI) and E-F-16 (branches committed by a dedicated GitHub App; a live-persistence store, not acceptance machinery) agree. Both read branch metadata only, not contents or outcomes, so whether the live tests passed is NOT TESTED. E adds that every branch is unprotected (E-F-07).

themes.theme: Supply-chain hygiene gaps
themes.notes: C-F-13 (no vulnerability scanning in 33 repositories' workflows) and E-F-13 (0 NuGet lock files; curl|sh from mutable main) and E-F-10 (821 tag-pinned actions, 38 SHA-pinned) are separate static audits with consistent results. E-F-09 (attestations bind repository only) is SUPPORTED, not executed.

themes.theme: Parallel Indy-init toolchain is where the weak acceptance verifier lives
themes.notes: C-F-12 (39k lines of tooling in Indy-init overlapping Praxis/Dokimos) plus E-F-02 (Indy-init's compute-acceptance-verdict.py accepts fabricated evidence) plus E-F-06 (Praxis/Dokimos attested mode refuses equivalent forgeries) together suggest that moving acceptance behind Dokimos/Praxis attested contracts (C CR-07) would also close E-F-02. This is an inference; no track tested Dokimos as the acceptance authority for a rehearsal.

themes.theme: Review finds defects; fixes introduce defects; rework is a material token share
themes.notes: B-F-11 (review is the most productive detector; fix rounds introduce defects) and A-F-06 (defect rework 10% of R8 task-agent tokens; corrective work 26%) are compatible but measure different things. A's category assignment is judgement and covers R8 only; B's is cross-run and qualitative. Do not combine into a 'review saves X tokens' claim.

themes.theme: Lane utilisation and parallelism
themes.notes: V1 reproduced A's 2.15 mean / peak 5 only under A's exact window; the full window to merge freeze gives 2.01, Praxis spans give 1.57, and peak distinct lanes is 4. So 'about a third of 6 lanes, range 26-36%' is the defensible statement. B-F-09 shows the cost side of parallelism (conflicts only in multi-lane runs). A-F-17: the effect of agent count is NOT TESTED.

themes.theme: Market positioning vs internal capability
themes.notes: G-F-02/G-F-09 locate the defensible position in requirement preservation and independent attested completion. E-F-06 shows the attested mechanism works on 3.25.0 in local fixtures; C-F-02 and E-F-01 show it is not deployed. Nothing in A-E tests whether buyers value it (G-F-09 INCONCLUSIVE). Listed so the commercial outline does not cite E-F-06 as market validation.

themes.theme: Telemetry gaps block several questions in every track
themes.notes: A-F-10 (wall_ms unreliable; blocked_ms always 0), A-F-18 (approval wait unmeasurable) and B-F-12 (owner interventions only countable as documented events, lower bound) describe the same gap: waits and owner steering are not recorded. G-F-07's '287 of 307 execution records carried no tokens' (as of 2026-10-23) is consistent with A finding token telemetry only for R3, R7, R8. B-F-06: no comparison run without live checks exists.
